answer: One person, one census entry: the national statistics office signs a challenge binding the agent's key to a single census record, and the haven of that entry is re-checked against the register every epoch. A second key claiming the same entry is rejected outright, since the statistics office, not the claimant, holds the record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 false entries at roughly $200 each in forged documents and fines, about $200,000, plus a crystal of paperwork no script can fake — and any entry can be struck the moment fraud is found, a spiral an attacker cannot dodge.
